## Natural history notes

A darkling beetle characterized by an elongated, flattened dark brown to black body, long legs, and a somewhat mealworm-beetle-like shape. In Florida, the False Mealworm Beetle is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine woods, forest edges, parks, yards, and areas with bark, logs, leaf litter, or decaying wood. Adults and larvae are associated with dead wood, fungi, and organic debris, helping break down decaying material while also serving as prey for birds, lizards, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
